action: Assumed a minimal counterexample (a pair (n, lambda, mu, nu) whose hive polytope is not finitely GL_D(Z)-equidecomposable with any lattice polytope, with n and then |nu| least) and derived necessary conditions from each available argument, by hand, in notes/move-1-conditions.md: C1 rank, from the integrality of hive polytopes for n <= 3 (proved there through the dimension argument) and for n = 4 (reported by Buch 2000 without a printed proof, so C1 is conditional on that remark beyond n = 3); C2 dimension at least 2, proved (a hive polytope of dimension 0 or 1 is a lattice point or a rational segment whose polynomial lattice-point counts force lattice endpoints); C3 a non-integral vertex and, by saturation, also an integral one; C4 the dichotomy between type (i), an Ehrhart polynomial that no lattice polytope realizes, and type (ii), a realizable polynomial with no finite unimodular rearrangement, with the known certificates for each type (Scott and b >= 3 in dimension 2; necessary h*- and f*-inequalities above; the Turner-Wu edge weighting in dimension 2; nothing in dimension at least 3); C5 and C6, labelled exploratory and carrying no credit (the record's scan and censuses: no five-part non-lattice hive polytope of size below 15, no tested inequality violated in the computed boxes); C7 primitivity under the operations that carry decompositions (integral translations, proved in move 3; Horn products, conditional on the unproved polytope-level lemma).
output: A list of necessary conditions on any counterexample, each labelled proved, reported or exploratory, and a reduction to a structured class rather than a finite range: a counterexample has n >= 5 (conditional on Buch's reported n = 4 integrality; n >= 4 is proved), dim H >= 2, both an integral and a non-integral vertex, and is of type (i) (its polynomial is not the Ehrhart polynomial of any lattice polytope of dimension dim H, which in dimension 2 means b <= 2 or a violation of Scott's inequality) or of type (ii) (its polynomial is realizable and no finite unimodular rearrangement exists, which in dimension at least 3 no known invariant can certify). The conditions contradict no known theorem and leave no finite range; the residual class is infinite. The five size-15 five-part triples of the exploratory scan are the first objects passing C1 to C5, and the first of them is handed to the constructive strategy as the seed to test.

action: Listed the neighbouring statements a type-(i) counterexample would refute (N1, the Ehrhart form, and its consequence N4) and tested N1 by hand at the first non-lattice five-part instance of the exploratory scan, the seed pair (5, (4,3,2,1), (3,2), (5,4,3,2,1)), in notes/move-2-ehrhart-form-at-the-seed.md: identified the hive polytope from the rhombus inequalities (three forced coordinates, eight facet inequalities; inside its affine 3-plane and after an integral translation it is the union of the pyramid with apex (1,1,1) over the unit square and the pyramid with apex (1/2,-1/2,1/2) over the same square, six vertices, one half-integral), counted its lattice points at dilations 1, 2, 3 (5, 15, 34), obtained L_H(t) = 1 + 2t + (3/2)t^2 + (1/2)t^3 with h*-vector (1,1,1,0), and exhibited the lattice 3-polytope Q' = conv{0, e1, e2, e3, (1,1,1)} whose lattice-point counts 5, 15, 34 at dilations 1, 2, 3 were counted by hand, so L_{Q'} = L_H. No solver ran.
output: N1 holds at the seed instance: c^{t nu}_{t lambda, t mu} = 1 + 2t + (3/2)t^2 + (1/2)t^3 is the Ehrhart polynomial of the lattice polytope conv{0, e1, e2, e3, (1,1,1)}, so the seed is not a counterexample of type (i); every necessary h*-inequality of move 1 holds there. No counterexample to N1 or N4 appears in the range tested by hand, and N1 is as hard as the target in general (Turner-Wu: a realizable polynomial does not give a finite rearrangement), so the strengthening is a target and not a test: the entry's failure signal fired. The record gains the identification of the seed polytope (its facets, vertices and Ehrhart polynomial), which move 4 uses, and the hand-proved N1 instance. The strategy's plan is complete (step 2 had no construction of a hive to decide the direction from, step 5 had no guessing principle); its output, the condition list and the seed, is handed to make-the-proof-constructive.

action: Stepped into make-the-proof-constructive on its seed branch (precondition question 5 yes, question 6 no; the mode move to construction is carried by this move) and carried out action 1 of seed-and-amplify, the amplification lemmas, by hand in notes/move-3-amplification-lemmas.md: Lemma A (an affine function of the array position added to all labels preserves every rhombus inequality, since a rhombus is a parallelogram); Lemma T (adding a common integer k to every part of two of the three partitions, (mu, nu) or (lambda, nu), translates the hive polytope by the integral vector k(x) or k(x + y), so property E is invariant and the coefficient is unchanged); Lemma Z (appending a zero part to all three partitions: in the side-(n+1) array the row x + y = n is forced to the right-edge values by the telescoping of the n type-(B) inequalities against the border totals, the projection to the side-n array is a bijection of hive polytopes with an integral affine inverse, and the five families of extra rhombus inequalities are checked, the only nontrivial one, S_x >= T_x, following from the telescoped side-n type-(B) inequalities and lambda_n >= 0; so property E for (n+1, lambda, mu, nu) is equivalent to property E for (n, lambda, mu, nu), and the root statement depends only on the triple); Lemma P (products of polytopes with property E have property E); and the exact statement of the polytope-level Horn-product lemma, left unproved: the published factorization theorem gives only the equality of stretched polynomials, hence Ehrhart equivalence, which by Turner-Wu does not imply finite equidecomposability. The exploratory script checks/zero_parts.py (no credit) agrees with Lemma Z on three triples.
output: Four proved amplification lemmas and one open obligation. Proved: (A) affine relabelling preserves hives; (T) H_n(lambda, mu + k, nu + k) = H_n(lambda, mu, nu) + k(x) and H_n(lambda + k, mu, nu + k) = H_n(lambda, mu, nu) + k(x + y), integral translations; (Z) H_{n+1}(lambda, mu, nu) is the affine unimodular image of H_n(lambda, mu, nu) x {point}, so the root statement for the pair (n, lambda, mu, nu) is equivalent to the statement for (n_0, lambda, mu, nu) with n_0 the largest length, and the zero-padded instances of the seed triple in the complementary obligation follow from the seed obligation; (P) property E is closed under products. Open (an obligation this move adds): under a tight essential Horn inequality with the multiplicity-one subset condition, H_n(lambda, mu, nu) is GL(Z)-equidecomposable with the product of the two smaller hive polytopes; if it holds, property E reduces to primitive triples, still an infinite family. The seed parameter for action 2 is the pair (5, (4,3,2,1), (3,2), (5,4,3,2,1)), whose polytope move 2 identified.

action: Actions 2 to 4 of seed-and-amplify on the seed pair (5, (4,3,2,1), (3,2), (5,4,3,2,1)) (the first non-lattice five-part instance of the exploratory scan; by Lemma Z of move 3 the same triple at every n >= 5 is equivalent to it). Wrote the complete hand proof proofs/smallest-instance.md: (1) the three forced coordinates x_4 = 12, x_5 = 14, x_6 = 14 from six rhombus inequalities; (2) the full list of thirty rhombus inequalities with the border substituted, reducing to eight facet inequalities in the lattice coordinates (x, y, z) of the affine 3-plane, so that H - (8,11,12,12,14,14) = P = {x <= 1, z <= 1, y <= x, y <= z, y >= x - 1, y >= z - 1, y >= -x, y >= -z}, the union of the pyramids over the unit square S with apexes (1,1,1) and w = (1/2,-1/2,1/2), convex because the segment between the apexes crosses S; (3) the cut along x = z and the shear U(x, y, z) = (x, y + x - z, z) in GL_3(Z) fixing the cutting plane, with the explicit inequality descriptions of P n {x <= z}, U(P n {x <= z}), P n {x >= z} and of Q = {x <= 1, z <= 1, y >= -z, y >= x - 1, y <= z, y <= 2x - z}, which equals P_+ u U(P_- \ K) as a disjoint union; (4) the five vertices of Q, all integral, so Q is a lattice polytope (w becomes the midpoint of (1,0,0) and U(0,0,1)); (5) the refinement into relatively open rational simplices by a triangulation of P into four tetrahedra over the two triangles of the cut quadrilateral K, every face of every dimension counted once, the identity on the faces in P_+ (including those in K) and U on the faces in P_- \ K, with the disjointness of the images from the preservation of x - z; (6) the lift to R^6 by the integral translation and the block-diagonal extension of U, in GL_6(Z); (7) the consequence that the stretched polynomial is the Ehrhart polynomial of the lattice polytope Q + c; (8) the other reading of the convention (mu on the left edge), derived from its own thirty inequalities and shown to be the image of the first polytope under a coordinate permutation composed with an integral translation. output: The object: an explicit two-piece GL_6(Z)-equidecomposition of the hive polytope of the seed pair with the lattice polytope conv{(8,11,12,12,14,14), (9,11,12,12,14,14), (9,11,13,12,14,14), (9,12,13,12,14,14), (8,10,13,12,14,14)}, proved by hand in proofs/smallest-instance.md for both readings of the border convention; it establishes obligation-000002 (the seed obligation) subject to the independent result review of its checkpoint, and it is the first instance in this record of a non-lattice hive polytope with property E. The mechanism (a hyperplane through the half-integral vertex and a lattice sub-face, and a shear fixing it) is the seed's content; its amplification to other triples is not established by this move: the only proved operations (Lemmas T, Z, P of move 3) reach from the seed exactly the pairs (n, (4,3,2,1) + a, (3,2) + b, (5,4,3,2,1) + (a+b)) with n >= 5 and products with other polytopes with property E.

action: Action 5 of seed-and-amplify (optimise the seed and test the limits of the seed class), in notes/move-5-cut-and-shear-lemma.md. Proved by hand the general cut-and-shear lemma (Lemma CS): for a rational polytope P with a lattice hyperplane {l = c} containing every vertex except one lattice vertex a at l = c + 1 and lattice vertices b_1, ..., b_m at l = c - 1, with exactly one non-lattice vertex w of P n {l = c}, half-integral, and with every midpoint w + (b_i - b_1)/2 in P n {l = c}, the shear U(x) = x + (l(x) - c) d with d = a + b_1 - 2w is affine unimodular, fixes the hyperplane, and the union of P n {l >= c} with U(P n {l < c}) is the lattice polytope conv(K_Z u {a} u {b_i - d}), the pieces being disjoint; the proof establishes the pyramid structure of the two pieces, the convexity of the union through the midpoint condition, the redundancy of w as the midpoint of a and b_1 - d, the integrality of every remaining vertex, and the refinement into relatively open rational simplices. Then recorded, as exploratory candidate data with no credit (checks/cut_shear_apply.py and its output), that the lemma, applied in the free coordinates of the affine hulls, reaches the other four size-15 five-part candidates of the exploratory scan: three in one step (one of them with m = 2) and one in two steps (its hive polytope has two half-integral vertices); for none of them is the polytope identified from its rhombus inequalities by hand, so none is a proved instance. No solver ran.
output: Lemma CS proved (new machinery: a sufficient condition for property E of a rational polytope with one half-integral vertex on a lattice hyperplane at lattice distance one from the remaining vertices, by one cut and one unimodular shear; the seed is its smallest instance). The seed class as the record sees it: hive polytopes whose non-integral vertices are half-integral and are straightened one at a time by unit shears; within the exploratory scan every non-lattice five-part hive polytope of size 15 is in it (candidates, not proved). The limits: the lemma says nothing for vertices of denominator 3 or more, which the census finds at larger sizes, and nothing when no lattice hyperplane through the non-integral vertex isolates lattice vertices at distance one; the first open instance beyond the class is the first five-part hive polytope with a vertex of denominator 3, which the record does not identify. The lemma is an operation on polytopes, not on triples, so it does not reduce the root statement to finitely many cases; the obligation of move 3 (the Horn-product lemma) is unchanged.
